newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-BASUKI GIVES INDONESIA BIG LIFT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BASUKI GIVES INDONESIA BIG LIFT.

text.p: Indonesian tennis took a giant leap on Tuesday when Yayuk Basuki became the first player from that country to reach the women's singles quarter-finals at Wimbledon, beating Canadian Patricia Hy-Boulais in straight sets.
"I feel great. It's a moment in history for Indonesian tennis," Basuki said.
"This is a major grand slam tournament, and no-one from Indonesia has ever been this far. For me this is something special. Hopefully my country is proud of me."
Basuki, who has reached the last 16 here four times but never before progressed to the final eight, overpowered the Canadian with her hard-hitting and brisk movement to the net to win 6-0 7-6 (7-2).
"I was playing well. She was quite nervous so I took the advantage," Basuki said.
The compact Indonesian cruised through the first set, but in the second Hy-Boulais threatened a comeback when she won three games in a row.
However, Hy-Boulais, 5-3 up and serving for the second set, failed to capitalise on her lead. Basuki's surge to the net and powerful return of serve cost the Canadian that game.
"She was serving for the set, she didn't take it and I felt a lot more positive," Basuki said.
Basuki started and finished the next game with an ace, while Hy-Boulais was clearly frustrated with her inability to move quickly enough after her serve.
"Move! Serve and move!," she coached herself.
Basuki maintained the momentum and polished off her opponent 7-2 in a speedy tie break.
But Basuki conceded Tuesday's game was no walkover.
"I had to be tough out there," she said. "I played ground strokes in the first three rounds, but today I needed to serve and volley."
The cheerful 26-year-old from Jakarta is just planning to enjoy the rest of the tournament. She faces a hard match in the last eight against either Mary Joe Fernandez or Jana Novotna.
"It's going to be a tough quarter-final but I have nothing to lose. I'm doing good, I feel great, and everything's going well."
She added: "I do well at Wimbledon. I love the atmosphere. It's one of my favourite places to play," she said.
Basuki became the first Indonesian to win a professional event at the 1991 Volvo Ladies Open.
